newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open higher Friday in line with the bullion market overnight where gold and palladium firmed.

The OTC options expiry in London Monday was said to be providing gold with some support, while news Russian officials had visited Japan without concluding any new platinum group metal supply agreement lifted palladium prices overnight.
COMEX June gold was called up $0.50 to $1.00 from Thursday's close of $342.70 an ounce after trading from $342.40 to $344.50 on ACCESS.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted early at $342.25/75 against the London morning fix of $341.35 and Thursday's New York close of $340.50/$341.00.
COMEX gold stocks slipped 96 ounces Thursday to 951,010 ounces. Silver stocks fell 16,868 ounces to 189,495,766 ounces.
COMEX July silver, now the more active contract, was called unchanged to up 0.5 cent from the previous close of $4.741. May silver's first notice day is April 30.
NYMEX July platinum was called up $0.50 to $1.00 from Thursday's close of $375.80, with NYMEX June palladium called up $1.00 to $2.00 from the prior close of $155.45.

Overnight, Russian central bank officials visited Japanese trade houses to talk about the marketing of platinum gorup metals. The bank officials were told how much metal the trade houses hoped to buy from Russia but no export contracts were signed.
